prompts: If I already run weave.Evaluation on a fixed dataset, why would I also configure Signals, and how can I limit what the Signal scores?

output.answer:
**Short answer:** Signals score the agent turns that show up in your project's Agents view. The docs I found don't say how that relates to `weave.Evaluation` on a fixed dataset, so the "why" below is partly my inference. You can limit what a custom signal scores with filters and a sample rate.

**Why add Signals**
- Signals appear in the Agents view's Signals tab. They show tags and ratings for your agent's conversations, and they flag quality and safety problems such as user frustration or NSFW content [S2].
- The Signals table lists scored turns from your agent. Each row shows the scorer, the last message, the agent, the score, a trend, and when it was scored [S5].
- My searches did not find a page that compares `weave.Evaluation` with Signals. My inference, not a documented statement, is this: a fixed dataset covers only the cases you put in it. Signals score the turns your agent handles, so they can surface things your dataset doesn't contain.
- I did not find a documented way to run Signals over a fixed dataset. I only found them described for agent turns.

**How to limit what a custom signal scores**
When you create a custom signal in **Agents → Signals → New signal → Custom Signal**, open **Advanced** and use these options [S1]:
1. **Only score turns matching**: add filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. If you leave it empty, the signal scores every agent turn. Multiple filters combine with `AND` [S1].
2. **Sample rate**: set the fraction of matching turns that get scored. Lower it for high-traffic agents to reduce cost [S1].
3. **Include tool calls**: this controls whether the turn's tool calls are sent to the scoring model as context [S1].

You can toggle, edit, or delete active signals later from the active-signals drawer [S6].

**Caveats**
- These options come from the custom-signal page. I did not check whether preset signals expose the same fields.
- Ingest sampling is a separate setting for self-managed Weave deployments. It never samples evaluations from the Weave SDK [S3].

**Next step:** Create a custom signal and start with a narrow **Only score turns matching** filter. Then add a **Sample rate** if volume or cost is a concern.

# Monitor your agents with signals

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

In Weave's [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md), the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Signals surface quality and safety issues to flag problems, find patterns, and highlight the traces that need your attention. Use signals to automatically score the quality of your agent's responses, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content.

To score turns with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score agent turns with a remote scorer](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/remote-scorer-signals.md).

sources.title: Monitor your agents with signals
sources.heading: Signals table
sources.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

sources.text:
## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

sources.title: Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed
sources.heading: What ingest sampling applies to
sources.text:
## What ingest sampling applies to

Ingest sampling applies to two kinds of traffic, and the rate you set applies to both:

* Calls from the `@weave.op` decorator, which appear in the **Traces** tab.
* Agent spans sent to the agent tracing endpoint (`/agents/otel/v1/traces`), which appear in the **Agents** tab. For more information, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

The following traffic is never sampled and is always kept in full:

* Evaluations from the Weave SDK. Weave keeps these because they are deliberate quality measurements, and their scores would be wrong if computed over partial data.
* Traces sent with your own OpenTelemetry tooling to the raw OTel endpoint (`/otel/v1/traces`). Raw OpenTelemetry traffic carries no evaluation marker, so sampling it could silently drop evaluations. For more information, see [Send OpenTelemetry traces to Weave](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/otel.md).
* Calls from Weave SDK versions earlier than the supported versions. See [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

# Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed

> Keep only a share of incoming traces to control storage and LLM scoring costs on a self-managed Weave instance

Ingest sampling lets you control the share of traces that arrive at a [self-managed Weave instance](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/platform/weave-self-managed.md) and drop the rest. This can help alleviate storage and processing costs for high-volume clusters by only keeping a specified percentage of traces.

This guide walks you through how to enable the feature on your self-managed Weave instance.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Ingest sampling requires a Weave server version that includes the sampler. Sampling of `@weave.op` calls also requires the Weave Python SDK 0.53.0 or later, or the Weave TypeScript SDK 0.16.0 or later. Agent spans have no SDK requirement. For details, see [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

Ingest sampling is independent of client-side sampling. The `tracing_sample_rate` parameter in the `@weave.op` decorator still lets an individual traced function sample its own calls, but only a server-side rate applies across the whole deployment and can't be changed or ignored by individual clients. For more information, see [Control sampling rate](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/ops.md#control-sampling-rate).

## What ingest sampling applies to

Ingest sampling applies to two kinds of traffic, and the rate you set applies to both:

* Calls from the `@weave.op` decorator, which appear in the **Traces** tab.
* Agent spans sent to the agent tracing endpoint (`/agents/otel/v1/traces`), which appear in the **Agents** tab. For more information, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

The following traffic is never sampled and is always kept in full:

* Evaluations from the Weave SDK. Weave keeps these because they are deliberate quality measurements, and their scores would be wrong if computed over partial data.
* Traces sent with your own OpenTelemetry tooling to the raw OTel endpoint (`/otel/v1/traces`). Raw OpenTelemetry traffic carries no evaluation marker, so sampling it could silently drop evaluations. For more information, see [Send OpenTelemetry traces to Weave](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/otel.md).
* Calls from Weave SDK versions earlier than the supported versions. See [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

# Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed

> Keep only a share of incoming traces to control storage and LLM scoring costs on a self-managed Weave instance

Ingest sampling lets you control the share of traces that arrive at a [self-managed Weave instance](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/platform/weave-self-managed.md) and drop the rest. This can help alleviate storage and processing costs for high-volume clusters by only keeping a specified percentage of traces.

This guide walks you through how to enable the feature on your self-managed Weave instance.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Ingest sampling requires a Weave server version that includes the sampler. Sampling of `@weave.op` calls also requires the Weave Python SDK 0.53.0 or later, or the Weave TypeScript SDK 0.16.0 or later. Agent spans have no SDK requirement. For details, see [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

Ingest sampling is independent of client-side sampling. The `tracing_sample_rate` parameter in the `@weave.op` decorator still lets an individual traced function sample its own calls, but only a server-side rate applies across the whole deployment and can't be changed or ignored by individual clients. For more information, see [Control sampling rate](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/ops.md#control-sampling-rate).

## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

Weave offers monitors with built-in signals: preset scorers that evaluate production traces for common quality issues and errors by default, with no custom setup. ## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

result.heading: What ingest sampling applies to
result.text:
## What ingest sampling applies to

Ingest sampling applies to two kinds of traffic, and the rate you set applies to both:

* Calls from the `@weave.op` decorator, which appear in the **Traces** tab.
* Agent spans sent to the agent tracing endpoint (`/agents/otel/v1/traces`), which appear in the **Agents** tab. For more information, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

The following traffic is never sampled and is always kept in full:

* Evaluations from the Weave SDK. Weave keeps these because they are deliberate quality measurements, and their scores would be wrong if computed over partial data.
* Traces sent with your own OpenTelemetry tooling to the raw OTel endpoint (`/otel/v1/traces`). Raw OpenTelemetry traffic carries no evaluation marker, so sampling it could silently drop evaluations. For more information, see [Send OpenTelemetry traces to Weave](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/otel.md).
* Calls from Weave SDK versions earlier than the supported versions. See [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

# Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed

> Keep only a share of incoming traces to control storage and LLM scoring costs on a self-managed Weave instance

Ingest sampling lets you control the share of traces that arrive at a [self-managed Weave instance](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/platform/weave-self-managed.md) and drop the rest. This can help alleviate storage and processing costs for high-volume clusters by only keeping a specified percentage of traces.

This guide walks you through how to enable the feature on your self-managed Weave instance.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Ingest sampling requires a Weave server version that includes the sampler. Sampling of `@weave.op` calls also requires the Weave Python SDK 0.53.0 or later, or the Weave TypeScript SDK 0.16.0 or later. Agent spans have no SDK requirement. For details, see [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

Ingest sampling is independent of client-side sampling. The `tracing_sample_rate` parameter in the `@weave.op` decorator still lets an individual traced function sample its own calls, but only a server-side rate applies across the whole deployment and can't be changed or ignored by individual clients. For more information, see [Control sampling rate](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/ops.md#control-sampling-rate).

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

sources.heading: Signals table
sources.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

sources.heading: What ingest sampling applies to
sources.text:
## What ingest sampling applies to

Ingest sampling applies to two kinds of traffic, and the rate you set applies to both:

* Calls from the `@weave.op` decorator, which appear in the **Traces** tab.
* Agent spans sent to the agent tracing endpoint (`/agents/otel/v1/traces`), which appear in the **Agents** tab. For more information, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

The following traffic is never sampled and is always kept in full:

* Evaluations from the Weave SDK. Weave keeps these because they are deliberate quality measurements, and their scores would be wrong if computed over partial data.
* Traces sent with your own OpenTelemetry tooling to the raw OTel endpoint (`/otel/v1/traces`). Raw OpenTelemetry traffic carries no evaluation marker, so sampling it could silently drop evaluations. For more information, see [Send OpenTelemetry traces to Weave](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/otel.md).
* Calls from Weave SDK versions earlier than the supported versions. See [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

# Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed

> Keep only a share of incoming traces to control storage and LLM scoring costs on a self-managed Weave instance

Ingest sampling lets you control the share of traces that arrive at a [self-managed Weave instance](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/platform/weave-self-managed.md) and drop the rest. This can help alleviate storage and processing costs for high-volume clusters by only keeping a specified percentage of traces.

This guide walks you through how to enable the feature on your self-managed Weave instance.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Ingest sampling requires a Weave server version that includes the sampler. Sampling of `@weave.op` calls also requires the Weave Python SDK 0.53.0 or later, or the Weave TypeScript SDK 0.16.0 or later. Agent spans have no SDK requirement. For details, see [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

Ingest sampling is independent of client-side sampling. The `tracing_sample_rate` parameter in the `@weave.op` decorator still lets an individual traced function sample its own calls, but only a server-side rate applies across the whole deployment and can't be changed or ignored by individual clients. For more information, see [Control sampling rate](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/ops.md#control-sampling-rate).

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

## Available signals

Weave offers monitors with built-in signals: preset scorers that evaluate production traces for common quality issues and errors by default, with no custom setup. Each built-in signal uses a benchmarked LLM prompt to classify traces and saves the results as comma-delimited tags representing the detected issues.

Signals use a [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) model to score traces, so you don't need external API keys.

Weave provides 13 preset signals organized into two groups.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

# Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed

> Keep only a share of incoming traces to control storage and LLM scoring costs on a self-managed Weave instance

Ingest sampling lets you control the share of traces that arrive at a [self-managed Weave instance](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/platform/weave-self-managed.md) and drop the rest. This can help alleviate storage and processing costs for high-volume clusters by only keeping a specified percentage of traces.

This guide walks you through how to enable the feature on your self-managed Weave instance.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Ingest sampling requires a Weave server version that includes the sampler. Sampling of `@weave.op` calls also requires the Weave Python SDK 0.53.0 or later, or the Weave TypeScript SDK 0.16.0 or later. Agent spans have no SDK requirement. For details, see [Requirements and limitations](#requirements-and-limitations).

Ingest sampling is independent of client-side sampling. The `tracing_sample_rate` parameter in the `@weave.op` decorator still lets an individual traced function sample its own calls, but only a server-side rate applies across the whole deployment and can't be changed or ignored by individual clients. For more information, see [Control sampling rate](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/ops.md#control-sampling-rate).

result.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.
